note: Agent-written (Claude Opus 5.5, 2026-10-26). Rules are first-class concepts on the 'rules' sheet: each names its kind, the concepts it governs, where it was stated, and aliases used to find further evidence. Bridges ('connecting elements') name the specific shared element that joins concepts across mediums. Evidence counts are measured by matching; the rule and bridge statements are the agent's reading of the cited sources.

rules.statement: Foreground frames, midground holds the character and focal point, background sets the scene; each plane has one job.
rules.source: Eyecager Sketchbook zine (studies/st-amberbladejones-2114453581625729120)

rules.statement: Horizon placement and mass size make or break a vertical frame; a 50/50 split is a hard sell and equal masses feel the same.
rules.source: Eyecager Sketchbook zine

rules.statement: Pattern colour temperature at the macro level (cool sky, warm ground) and alternate it at the micro level; put red in foliage shadows.
rules.source: Eyecager Sketchbook zine, crediting a Ghibli background painter; measured shadow a* +6.2 against lit green -4.9

rules.statement: Neutral pose, camera and background connect to a character; dynamic ones build tension; mixing them carelessly causes dissonance.
rules.source: Eyecager Sketchbook zine

rules.statement: Readability is king: contrast serves separation and the focal point before poetry.
rules.source: Eyecager Sketchbook zine ('Readability is King'); lettering PROGRESS readability passes

rules.statement: One hot mark per view; colour is verdict-only in UI.
rules.source: design canon (CLAUDE.md, DESIGN-VOICE-CANON); matched by rileycx's single orange (0.4% to 28% of a view)

rules.statement: No taglines, helper text or secondary labels; if a screen needs them, redesign it.
rules.source: Synthesis-and-Design-Framework.md

rules.statement: Two type families only, one grotesk and one mono; hierarchy from weight and size.
rules.source: design canon (Hanken Grotesk + Conso)

rules.statement: Break every reference into parts and recombine them into our own system; never copy piecewise.
rules.source: Synthesis-and-Design-Framework.md

rules.statement: Tesserae are laid in courses (andamento) that follow the form's contour, so the flow of the tiles describes the shape.
rules.source: name-art/lib/mosaic/andamento.mjs header; Byzantine mosaic practice

rules.statement: Erosion should follow local stroke width so thin parts of a letter survive.
rules.source: name-art/README.md and DECISIONS.md (the r collapses otherwise)

rules.statement: In intaglio, tone comes from line density and width under a raking light, never from flat fill; the edge exists where cuts end.
rules.source: name-art 16-intaglio-lines; techniques/lib/burin.js

rules.statement: Fix the time (a 30-minute lock) so the study gets finished; the time becomes part of the work ('Done in mm:ss').
rules.source: 30desk.art via @love-kirby and @Ramon_N90

rules.statement: Physical imperfection (ink spread, paper grain, registration error) makes motion feel alive.
rules.source: gwamoleipstop printed motion (post text); Divisumma 26's '13345'

rules.statement: A dye spreads with radius growing as the square root of time (r ~ t^0.5); a moving front grows linearly.
rules.source: physics; measured spread exponents 0.15 to 0.40 in this batch (refdb/flowmeasure.py)

rules.statement: Evaporating liquid carries suspended pigment to the drying edge and leaves it there as a rim.
rules.source: physics; Frankenthaler's blot rims; pigment-rivulet tide lines

rules.statement: Overlapping transparent inks multiply their transmissions; real inks absorb outside their band, so the ideal multiply misses hue.
rules.source: Olivetti 'De A à Z' test: multiply ΔE 14 to 21, opaque ΔE 70 to 92 (lib/tools/overprint_test.py)

rules.statement: Light through a medium falls off exponentially with depth, red first in water.
rules.source: physics; Kitada Aya's underwater paintings; cloud2d.js Beer march

rules.statement: Light bends at an interface by the ratio of refractive indices; from under water the sky shows as a window of half-angle 48.6 degrees.
rules.source: physics; Kitada Aya study

rules.statement: A shape sets its resonances, but the resonances do not always fix the shape (Kac 1966; Gordon, Webb and Wolpert 1992).
rules.source: mathelirium study (from memory, high confidence)

rules.statement: A thin layer reflects colours that interfere constructively at its thickness; the hue walks with thickness and angle.
rules.source: physics; feed set 20 light-leak study; Begonia pavonina

rules.statement: A yield-stress paint flows only where pushed past its yield value and holds ridges elsewhere.
rules.source: pecelnya brush spiral (coherence 0.82)

rules.statement: Keep the third thin or absent; the minor colour comes from a fifth plus a flat sixth.
rules.source: 2026-10-23-music-archive/THEME-BRIEF.md

rules.statement: Make the flat sixth (bVI, or b6 over the pedal) the main colour move; lead cells repeat one colour tone (5, b6 or 9).
rules.source: THEME-BRIEF.md

rules.statement: The pad dips about 6 dB under each kick (5.9 dB on 92% of kicks in Stolie): separation by ducking.
rules.source: THEME-BRIEF.md

rules.statement: The room is a dark 1 to 2 s space with one wide return; harmony low-passed under about 1 kHz with slow attacks; drums carry the only brightness.
rules.source: THEME-BRIEF.md

rules.statement: Perceived change follows the ratio, not the difference: each added transparent layer reads as a smaller step, so a fifth layer barely reads darker (Albers, Interaction of Color, plate XX-1).
rules.source: Albers, Interaction of Color, plate XX-1 (BugNews save 2026-10-25). One shared measurement, measures/albers-xx1.json (lib/tools/albers_xx1.py: superframe sheet boxes, 8 px edge exclusion, median sRGB to CIE Lab D65; fits on unclipped depths 1 to 4): L* steps [-10.62, -2.99, -0.8, -0.09], dE steps [71.05, 5.9, 1.52, 1.0] (the first uses clipped paper), L* fits ln(depth) better than depth (rmse 0.454 vs 0.744)

rules.statement: A video's colour comes from the grade after shooting, not from the camera alone.
rules.source: mangoddango save, 2026-10-25 (Korean post: colour is not just good shooting, post-correction matters)

rules.statement: Split an argument into premises, presuppositions and conclusions; read conjunctions as turns or continuations; mark the movements (chain, list, turn) so the whole can be rebuilt. The same decomposition the art studies use, applied to text.
rules.source: Aliocha (@4liocha_), studies/st-4liocha_-2114086943776448820; lens probe: 7 of 7 breaks start at a connective in the Latin

rules.statement: Art deco builds from a closed motif set (fan, feather, fountain, palm, peacock, scallop, sunburst, waves, volute, clouds, chevron, aircraft fin) stepped and mirrored about an axis, with light as a material (floodlit towers, the Chrysler crown).
rules.source: gietzschean threads, 2026-10-26 (motif list and examples: O'Keeffe's Radiator Building, the Chrysler crown, a Persian lacquered fan); feeds name-art's deco and the type engine

bridges.statement: The dark edge left where a liquid stops: a soak-stain rim, an ink bloom's edge, a beach's wrack line, sediment in the medium.
The unit that carries one piece of the whole: Olivetti's blocks and ribbon tiles, Byzantine tesserae, Martens' glyph cells, a story beat in a sequence.
A translucent layer: Pink Noise's acetate, an overprint ink, a depth plane, a sound layer under a kick.
One continuous mark carried by a hand or a flow: a brush spiral, a burin cut, a one-stroke dragon, a letter's skeleton.
The small random texture of a medium: paper tooth, film grain, pigment granulation, the noise floor.
A single bright reflection from a tilted facet: sun glitter on waves, a highlight on glass, a specular dot.
A closed loop that spreads or holds: a ripple, a drum's nodal circle, an iris, a halo.
A line that joins: a sewing thread, a network edge, a rope strand, a ribbon.
An opening that frames and bends what is seen: Snell's window, the eye, a frame within a frame, a grey rectangle in a flower.
A unit of liquid added to a medium: a pigment drop, an ink drop in water, a raindrop, a kick that ducks the pad.
The moving edge between two states: an ink-bloom reveal, a style infection across a grid, a wave front, a burn line.
Time laid out as cells: a contact sheet, a temporal mosaic, a 30desk wall of timed studies, numbered steps.
The cut between parts that lets a whole be taken apart and rebuilt: an I-beam mark between premises, a grout line between tesserae, a cut in a recut film, a seam in a parts tree.
